budget.rationale: Replace the two one-way sum with the $6,733 complete family option; allow $720 bags and $200–800 seats, rounded up to $7,700–8,300. Add a previously missing $500–900 insurance/contingency allowance (estimate). Gross $14,200–$18,300 less a single $2,000 fixed travel redemption yields $12,200–$16,300. Budget 1/5 follows the manifest; unresolved quotes prevent the high-confidence 3/5 exception.

weather.rationale: June is predominantly dry and warm; early starts manage exposed archaeology, gorge and fortress days.

fireRisk.rationale: Greece is inside official fire season in June; wind, gorge access and road closure create moderate disruption exposure with three-base flexibility.

swim.rationale: The itinerary schedules repeated natural-water days in the 73–74°F planning range, with multiple wind-direction alternatives.

variety.rationale: Substantial water, town/food, gorge/nature and archaeology/history modes are all scheduled.

ease.rationale: One island, no internal flight and the new one-stop outbound help, but three bases, two lodging moves, a two-stop return and several full driving days keep logistics moderate.

food.rationale: All three bases and remote days have named plain-food, grocery and apartment-kitchen fallbacks.

risk.rationale: Exact-date inventory exists, but final ticket protection and several 2027 activity access rules remain open.

nights.rationale: Thirteen hotel nights derive 5/5 under the shared rubric.

novelty.rationale: Crete is new, but the family has visited several Greek islands, so this is mostly new with a familiar destination type.

pto.rationale: Nine PTO days derive 2/5 and have zero default weight.
